So Go is a 19 x 19 board meaning there are 361 different places you can place a stone. Once a player places a stone there are now 360 places left for the next player to place a stone. In this way an unpruned game tree would have 361! (or 361 x 360 x 359 x 358.... x 2) possible games. This figure would be around 10^768. However, through various pruning by ruling out illegal moves and a variety of other techniques they have gotten it down to around 10^360. The only way to really give you a handle on how big this number is is to say that imagine every atom in the universe had a universe inside of it and then every atom inside those nested universes had a universe inside of it and then every atom in that layer of universes in turn had a universe. So by nesting 3 layers of universes beyond our own universe, we would still be at (10^80)^4 which is 10^320 and still 10000000000000000000000000000000000000000 times smaller than the number of possible go games.
